summary: priority_support was added to the subscription model and a ratecard entry was created, but the billing regression suite failed: the new entitlement's invoice line is generated with a zero amount for a subset of business-tier subscriptions whose entitlement_flags were set before the ratecard entry existed, and the reprocessing path does not backfill them. Three tests fail and one is flaky under the new ordering.

diagnosis.explanation: The implementation followed the package as written, but the package does not document how an entitlement flag that already exists on a subscription is reconciled with a ratecard entry that is introduced later. The billing ledger prices each invoice line from the ratecard version in force at renews_at; the account model says a flag set to true means the entitlement is active 'regardless of the plan default', but neither document states what the ledger should do when a subscription's entitlement_flags reference an entitlement that has no ratecard entry for the cycle being priced. The agent produced code that emits a zero-amount line in that case, which is a defensible reading of the silence in the docs, and the regression suite encodes a different expectation (backfill/proration). This is a documentation gap, not obviously a code defect: the package under-specifies the propagation and reconciliation rules between account entitlement_flags and the versioned ratecard.
diagnosis.technical_details: Traced the failing path from data/account-model.md (entitlement_flags semantics) to data/billing-ledger.md (invoice line generation and ratecard versioning). account-model.md: 'A flag set to true means the entitlement is active on this subscription, regardless of whether the plan grants it by default.' billing-ledger.md: 'Always price a line from the ratecard version that was in force at renews_at, not today's.' Neither document defines: (a) whether a flag predating a ratecard entry is billed retroactively; (b) whether mid-cycle activation is prorated and by what basis; (c) whether reprocessing backfills lines created before a ratecard entry existed; (d) the identifier correspondence between an entitlement code in entitlement_flags and a ratecard_code. The agent searched all four package files and the index; no section covers reconciliation. The three failing tests each assert one of (a)/(b)/(c); the flaky test is sensitive to line-generation ordering, which is also unspecified.
recommendations: Add a 'Reconciliation' section to data/billing-ledger.md defining how entitlement_flags map to ratecard entries, including the case where a flag predates the ratecard entry.
State explicitly whether the entitlement code in entitlement_flags is the same identifier as ratecard_code, or whether an explicit mapping table is required.
Define the behaviour when a flag is active but no ratecard entry exists for the cycle: zero-amount line, skipped line, or error.
Specify mid-cycle activation semantics (proration basis, rounding, and whether the first partial cycle is charged).
Specify reprocessing/backfill rules: when a past cycle is re-run, are lines created for entitlements whose ratecard entry was added after the original run?
Document the ordering of invoice-line generation so results are deterministic and tests are not flaky.
Add a worked example: a business-tier subscription with priority_support activated before the ratecard entry, showing the expected invoice line for the following two cycles.
Clarify how plan_version and ratecard version interact when they advance independently.
State whether functional-only (non-billable) entitlements are ever expected to appear in reconciliation logs even though they produce no line.
Add acceptance-criteria wording to the task so a future run can be checked mechanically against these reconciliation rules.
